title: Tutor CoPilot: A Human-AI Approach for Scaling Real-Time Expertise
extended_summary:
This paper addresses whether a human-AI system can improve the quality and effectiveness of live K-12 tutoring by giving novice tutors real-time, expert-like guidance. The core problem is that novice educators often lack access to expensive expert coaching, which can limit the quality of instruction and particularly disadvantage students from under-served communities.

The intervention, Tutor CoPilot, is a language-model-based system integrated into a virtual tutoring platform. When tutors activate it during a session, it generates context-sensitive suggestions using the lesson topic, chat context, and a selected pedagogical strategy. The system was developed using a method that extracts expert reasoning from think-aloud data and adapts it for live use. Tutors could edit, regenerate, or switch strategies, so the tool functioned as a decision-support aid rather than an automated tutor.

The study was a randomized controlled trial with 900 tutors and 1,800 K-12 students in grades 3-8 from Title I schools in a large U.S. Southern school district, delivered through an in-school virtual tutoring program for mathematics. The paper finds that students whose tutors had access to Tutor CoPilot were 4 percentage points more likely to pass exit tickets, with larger gains for students working with lower-rated or less-experienced tutors. Text analysis of more than 550,000 messages suggests that treatment tutors used more high-quality pedagogical strategies, such as prompting explanation and asking guiding questions, and fewer answer-giving strategies. Tutors reported that the system was helpful but sometimes produced suggestions that were not well aligned to grade level.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a preregistered randomized controlled trial with tutor-level random assignment, a large sample, and clear outcome measures, which strongly supports causal inference. There are some relevance and implementation caveats, but the design is high quality for K-12 intervention evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: The main academic effect is modest but meaningful for a priority population: a 4 percentage point increase in exit-ticket mastery, with larger gains for lower-rated tutors (up to 9 points). This suggests practical promise, though the outcome is proximal and the longer-term test-score effects were not significant.

interventions.use_case: Human-AI real-time tutoring support that generates expert-like pedagogical suggestions for live K-12 math tutors during tutoring sessions, including hints, guiding questions, worked examples, and strategy selection to improve tutor responses.

finding.finding_summary: In a randomized controlled trial with 1,800 K-12 students and 4,136 tutoring sessions, students whose tutors had access to Tutor CoPilot were 4 percentage points more likely to pass their exit tickets (62% to 66%, p<0.01). Conditional on attempting the exit ticket, students were 3 percentage points more likely to pass (p<0.01), indicating improved proximal math mastery.
finding.measure: Exit ticket pass rate; exit ticket attempted; conditional exit ticket pass rate

finding.finding_summary: Student survey outcomes showed no statistically significant effects on perceived tutor care, confidence in learning math, or session ratings. Estimated treatment effects were small and mixed (e.g., -0.004 to 0.03 on 5-point survey items) and were not significant.
finding.measure: Post-session student survey responses (e.g., tutor cared about understanding, confidence learning math, preference for understanding over memorizing, session rating, tutor rating)

finding.finding_summary: Treatment tutors were more likely to use strategies associated with deeper understanding, such as prompting students to explain and asking questions to guide thinking. The paper reports these strategies were used approximately 2 standard deviations more frequently on a log-odds scale in treatment sessions, compared with control sessions.
finding.measure: NLP-classified tutoring strategy use in 550,000+ chat messages
finding.effect_size: ~2 SD on log-odds scale for key high-quality strategies

finding.finding_summary: The system was inexpensive to deploy, with an estimated annual cost of $20 per tutor based on observed usage patterns. The intervention is positioned as a scalable alternative to traditional professional development, and tutors reported that it reduced the effort needed to generate appropriate instructional language in real time.
finding.measure: Estimated annual cost per tutor; tutor-reported usability/effort
finding.study_size: n=900 tutors assigned; cost estimate based on usage
